OK-2026-SB2182.aiSummary: Creates a state law that lets a person sue if someone intentionally shares or threatens to share a private intimate image without consent. It covers people shown in those images and sets rules for when consent, privacy, and certain defenses apply, including cases involving parents, legal guardians, cloud and hosting providers, and matters of public concern. The law also allows damages, court costs, attorney fees, and other relief, and it became law after the governor approved it.

OK-2026-SB1531.aiSummary: The law gives the Oklahoma Department of Aerospace and Aeronautics more power to manage unmanned aircraft systems and advanced air mobility, which means new air tech and the needed support systems. It lets the department keep registries, study other states’ rules, apply for grants and test sites, and work with cities, counties, tribes, federal agencies, and other groups on infrastructure and testing. It also lets the department make rules to carry out the program. It takes effect November 1, 2026.

OK-2026-SB1090.aiSummary: The measure would change Oklahoma rules for the "Invest In Oklahoma" program, which lets public money be invested in private equity, venture capital, and growth funds. It would give the State Treasurer more of the job of picking and overseeing funds, set factors to use in that review, and require lists and reports on the program. It would also let certain state retirement and trust funds invest up to 5% of their assets in approved funds.

OK-2026-HB3021.aiSummary: The measure changes Oklahoma school curriculum and graduation rules, including a set 23-unit course plan for students in grades 8 through 12 starting in the 2025-2026 school year. It also changes some graduation paths, adds rules for online course waivers and school website notice, and lets certain military children meet the Oklahoma history requirement with a project or paper. State education and higher education agencies must also work together on a joint plan so courses meet graduation rules, and the measure was approved by the Governor.

OK-2026-SB2084.aiSummary: The measure sets a cap on payouts for wrongful termination claims against higher education institutions for faculty members. In those cases, the total paid to settle a claim, through settlement, arbitration, or court order, could not be more than two years of the faculty member’s base pay or contract benefits, and it would count back pay and other money damages. It would not count retirement contributions already earned or unpaid wages or leave already accrued. The act takes effect November 1, 2026.

OK-2026-SB1286.aiSummary: The bill requires certain school districts and towns or cities that held an election run by a county election board on or after January 1, 2023, to provide a room to use as a polling place if there is no suitable one nearby and the county election board asks for it in writing. The space must be in a school or municipal building and must be provided at no cost. It was approved by the governor and takes effect November 1, 2026.

OK-2026-HR1060.title: Resolution; impeachment; Chief Justice of the Oklahoma Supreme Court; findings.
OK-2026-HR1060.aiSummary: The resolution says the Oklahoma House should impeach Chief Justice Dustin Rowe of the Oklahoma Supreme Court. It says the basis is his conduct in relation to grand jury proceedings in Payne County, including claims of neglect of duty and corruption in office. It is a formal statement asking for impeachment under the Oklahoma Constitution.
